record.subjects: Spiritual gifts ; Philosophy & religion ; Derrida, Jacques, 1930-2004
record.abstract: The article examines the deconstructive focus of French philosopher Jacques Derrida (1930-2004) on the gift's purity and the aporia this entails and the discussion of primacy of givenness in phenomenology of religion.

record.title: RENÉ GIRARD'S THEORY OF SACRIFICE, OR: WHAT IS THE GIFT OF DEATH?
record.subjects: Sacrifice ; Violence & the Sacred (Book) ; Girard, René, 1923-2015
record.abstract: The article discusses a study by French historian René Girard (1923-2015) titled "Violence and the Sacred," which aspires to come to terms with human evil, to detect the main role of sacrifice for the functioning of human societal being, and to show the intimate relation of evil to the sacred.

record.title: INTRODUCTION: THE DIALOGICAL PROMISE OF MASHUP PHILOSOPHY OF RELIGION.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Mashups (Musical form) ; Philosophy & religion
record.abstract: An introduction is presented in which the editor discusses various reports within the issue on topics including the concept of mashup philosophy of religion, mashup music, and the challlenges that mashup philosophy might face as of March 2015.

record.title: A SHALLOW SPECIES IN DEEP TIME: MODERNISM, POSTMODERNISM, AND OUR PLACE IN THE POTENTIAL HISTORY OF INQUIRY.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Modernism (Christian theology) ; Postmodernism (Philosophy) ; Pessimism ; Deep time ; Humility
record.abstract: The article examines the role of deep time in motivating epistemic humility with regard to humans' place in time. Modernism and postmodernism are discussed which are two forms of the philosophy and situates them within the philosophy of religion. An overview of deep time is provided and explores the positive and negative aspects of modernism and post modernism. Also tackled are pessimism and optimism, intellectual humility and consilience, and continental and analytic religious philosophy.

record.title: HUMANIZING PHILOSOPHY OF RELIGION: ON LANGUAGE IN LEVINAS AND SELLARS.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Religious communities ; Ethics ; Theory of knowledge (Religion) ; Philosophy & religion ; Religious humanism
record.abstract: An essay is presented on the philosophy of religion (PoR) with regard to two orientations to the subject. These orientations are the claim that the PoR's purpose is to promote a set of absolute moral norms and the claim that the field aims to determine whether religious communities' practices are true. Also explored are the tendency of the PoR to enable a thinking subject to make true claims, the mashup PoR, and the canon of modern PoR.

record.title: ON THE ETHICAL BASIS OF LANGUAGE: SOME THEMES IN DAVIDSON, CAVELL, AND LEVINAS.
record.subjects: Language & languages ; Philosophy of religion ; Skepticism ; Ethics ; Davidson, Donald, 1917-2003 ; Cavell, Stanley, 1926-2018 ; Lévinas, Emmanuel, 1906-1995
record.abstract: An essay is presented on the views of three philosophers on the relationship between being a linguistic agent and an ethical agent with regard to the philosophy of religion. These philosophers are Donald Davidson, Stanley Cavell, and Emmanuel Levinas. Other topics include how understanding language needs community conceptualization, the relationship between language and ethics, and skepticism.

record.title: PROLEGOMENA TO ANY FUTURE MASHUPS WITH THE PHILOSOPHY OF RELIGION.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Theism ; Philosophy & religion ; Critical thinking ; God ; Philosophy ; Scholarly periodicals ; Commercial Printing (except Screen and Books) ; Other printing ; Periodical Publishers
record.abstract: An essay is presented on modern English-language philosophy of religion (PoR) with regard to its possible mashup with other disciplines and as a specialized discussion within philosophy. Topics include critical thinking, a mousetrap analogy that supports the theory that a theistic God exists, and the need for PoR to be transformed and reject classical theism. Also discussed are typical introductory religious studies classroom and introductory approaches of books and scholarly journals.

record.title: IS MASHUP THE RIGHT METAPHOR?
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Mashups (Musical form) ; Metaphor ; Critical thinking ; Philosophy & religion
record.abstract: The article examines mashups as a metaphor for conceptualizing philosophy of religion (PoR). The limitations of the mashup metaphor is explored as well as a critical inquiry method neglected by the mashup metaphor. It offers information on mashup music and proposes a metaphor that fosters productive thinking of PoR. Other topics include the diversity of religious phenomena, the analytic and continental modes of inquiry, and modern PoR.

record.title: PHILOSOPHY MASHED-UP AND IN CRISIS.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Mashups (Musical form) ; Philosophy & religion ; Auditing ; Neoliberalism ; Higher education
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on the meta-philosophy of mash-up philosophy of religion (PoR) based on the concept of mashup music. He explores his experience of undertaking a meta-philosophical journey as well as the failure of mash-up philosophy to address issues facing philosophy. Other topics include the auditing culture, the use of neoliberal principles in higher education, and the need for modern philosophers to practice outide conventional institutional boundaries.

record.title: FAITH: BELIEF OR PRACTICE?
record.subjects: Faith ; Philosophy of religion ; Belief & doubt ; Philosophical analysis ; Saints ; Logic
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on faith with regard to whether it is belief or practice and situates it within the philosophy of religion. The differences between analytical and continental methods of philosophical analysis are discussed as well as faith as a social phenomenon. Other topics include religious language, the conflict between faith and reason, and the features of saintliness.

record.title: MEETING MARY IN MYTH: PURSUING PRE/POST/MODERN APOLOGETICS.
record.subjects: Apologetics ; Religious thought ; Philosophy of religion ; Philosophy & religion ; Lewis, C. S., 1898-1963 ; Caputo, John
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on apologetics which is a sub-field of the philosophy of religion. Apologetics refer to writings that justify something or to reasoned arguments. The views of author C. S. Lewis on Christianity's division is explored as well as continental and analytical philosophies of religion. Other topics include philosopher John Caputo's views on the relationship between analytic and continental philosophy.

record.title: TO "LET RELIGION ITSELF SPEAK:" FEUERBACH AND RELIGIOUS CONSCIOUSNESS IN MODERN CULTURE.
record.subjects: Philosophy of religion ; Consciousness ; Religious studies ; On Religion: Speeches to Its Cultured Despisers (Book) ; Feuerbach, Ludwig, 1804-1872 ; Schleiermacher, Friedrich, 1768-1834
record.abstract: The article presents the author's views on philosopher Ludwig Feuerbach's opinion on religious conciousness in modern culture. Feuerbach's model of religious consciousness is explored which reportedly also demonstrates self-consciousness based on religious feeling. Other topics include the book "On Religion: Speeches to Its Cultured Despisers" by Friedrich Schleiermacher, the developments in religion and political philosophy studies, and debates in religious studies.

record.title: VERNACULAR FUNDAMENTALISM AFTER ŽIŽEK: SOME ETHICAL CONCERNS ABOUT RELIGIOUS ONLINE COMMUNICATION.
record.subjects: Religion & ethics ; Philosophy of religion ; Philosophers ; Virtual communications ; Žižek, Slavoj, 1949- ; Howard, Robert Glenn
record.abstract: An essay is presented on philosopher Slavoj Žižek's promotion of the need to examine the ethical aspects of religious online communication and on professor Robert Glenn Howard's case study, Digital Jesus. It compares both philosophers views on religious online communication and examines the role mashup philosophy of religion on the use of religious language in faith and politics. Also discussed is the nexus between immoralism, extremism, literalism, and dogmatism.

record.title: KNOWLEDGE, VIRTUE, AND ONTOTHEOLOGY: A KIERKEGAARDIAN (SELF-)CRITIQUE.
record.subjects: Faith ; Theology ; Philosophy of religion ; Philosophers ; Kierkegaard, Søren, 1813-1855
record.abstract: The article examines philosopher Soren Kierkegaarde's views on faith with regard to ontotheology, virtue, and knowledge. Several methods used by Kierkegaarde to discuss faith as an ethical state are explored to illustrate that they can be examined based on the virtue tradition. Also discussed are the continental tradition in philosophy, the philosophy of religion (PoR), and mashup PoR.
